actions.heading: What to do first, and why
paragraphs: First, check read frequency on the {F037} cold buckets and approve the archive-class move, because it carries the largest estimate, {O1.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month, on {F036} TiB. Second, confirm the {F034} TiB of duplicate candidates by content hash before deleting anything. Third, reconcile the {F033} unreadable buckets with the provider.

In parallel, prepare de-identified or aggregated copies for reference data and channel engagement. Database tidying, worth {O3.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month for cold tables, can run alongside but should not lead. Every move here is a proposal; nothing is authorised by this report.

chapter4.heading: First data products and what each needs
paragraphs: {F018} candidates were scored. Reference and master-data licensing, the content catalogue and recommendation corpus, and channel and telco engagement analytics lead, all at grade C. Reference data is the sensible first product because it can be reduced to canonical fields, and channel engagement is the natural second because it aggregates by channel and period.

Each needs personal-data markers handled by de-identification or aggregation, and cleansing of empty required fields. The customer segmentation, forecasting, transaction, geospatial and civic candidates carry more markers or weaker grades and should follow once cleansing has been shown to work.

chapter5.heading: What remains unmeasured
paragraphs: Measures cover {F003} of {F002} tables, which is {K001}. {F033} of {F032} buckets were unreadable. The file shares, at {F040} TiB, have no duplication measure. One database connection could not be read.

None of these gaps overturns the picture of where the bytes sit. They do bound the certainty of the saving estimates, which could rise or fall once the unreadable buckets and the file shares are brought into measurement.

compare.heading: Three priced moves side by side
paragraphs: Moving buckets not written for over a year to archive-class storage addresses {O1.reclaimable_gib} GiB and is estimated at {O1.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month. Reconciling duplicate objects addresses {O2.reclaimable_gib} GiB at {O2.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month. Moving cold tables addresses {O3.reclaimable_gib} GiB at {O3.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month.

All three are estimates at reference list prices. The first depends on read frequency, which was not measured, and archive-class retrieval carries its own fee. The second rests on name and size matching, which for multipart uploads is not a content hash. The third counts only tables with timestamp columns. Each is a proposal only; nothing has been authorised.

exhibit_S001.heading: Database bytes are concentrated in a few places
paragraphs: The largest databases hold {F016} GiB of the {F004} GiB in the databases, which is {K002}. One staging database dominates the series. Cleansing and cost effort can therefore be aimed at very few databases and still cover almost every database byte.
Staging copies may be deliberate, so retirement needs the owner's confirmation. The census sketches {F014} duplicate table pairs, but the overlap is an estimate and not a row-level comparison.

exhibit_S002.heading: Completeness is the dominant condition issue
paragraphs: Exact duplicate rows are {F007} of rows, a low figure. Degraded rows are {F008}, and rows with empty required-looking fields are {F009}. Personal-data markers appear in {F010} of the {F011} rows sampled.

Completeness is the main constraint on what can be offered to a buyer. The personal-data markers do not block a product; they define the preparation step, which is de-identification or aggregation before release.

exhibit_S003.heading: Reclaimable bytes are almost all in the object store
paragraphs: Bytes not written for over a year are {F036} TiB in the object store, which is {K009} of it. Separately, {F034} TiB are duplicate candidates, {F035} of objects, matched on name and size rather than content. The three largest strategies address {K004} of the bytes that all strategies reach.

Database strategies are comparatively minor. About {F005} GiB, {F006} of database bytes, looks reclaimable before pricing. They are worth doing for tidiness and risk reduction, but they will not change the cost position.

exhibit_S004.heading: The object store dominates the estate
paragraphs: Of the {F050} TiB held, the object store accounts for {F030} TiB and the file shares for {F040} TiB. The databases are a very small remainder, at {K007} of the estate. The estate-wide view therefore differs sharply from a database-only one, which would have shown {F004} GiB and missed almost everything.

For the owner this means database tuning cannot move the cost position materially. The object store, at {K005} of the estate, is where the bytes and the money sit, and the file shares, at {K006}, are the second place to look.

exhibit_S005.heading: Most of the object store sits in one bucket
paragraphs: The largest bucket holds {F038} TiB, which is {K008} of the object store. The next largest buckets are each a few TiB, and those listed as cold are the ones that matter for archive savings. The largest bucket is not marked cold in the listing.

The practical consequence is that the archive saving is spread across many mid-sized cold buckets, {F037} in all, rather than concentrated in one decision. The largest bucket deserves its own review of purpose and access, which this census does not provide.

risks.heading: What the evidence cannot yet establish
paragraphs: Condition ratios rest partly on samples, semantic similarity to the market is unmeasured, one database connection is unread, file-share duplication is unknown and {F033} buckets are unreachable. Each closes with a defined step: a complete-pass census, a buyer-side review, a read grant and re-census, a fingerprinting pass and a bucket inventory reconciled with the provider.
Savings are estimates at reference list prices, not realised returns, and the product candidates are not qualified or sealed datasets.

summary: The estate holds {F050} TiB, of which the object store is {K005} and the file shares {K006}. The {F001} databases, with {F002} tables and {F004} GiB, are {K007} of the bytes. Cost, therefore, sits outside the databases, and any estate-wide plan has to start with object and file storage.

The priced strategies bound the monthly saving at {F019} USD at reference list prices, not the owner's invoice. Nearly all of it comes from moving buckets not written for over a year to archive-class storage and from reconciling duplicate objects. Both are estimates and neither has been confirmed against read patterns or content hashes.

Database rows are seldom duplicated but often incomplete: {F009} have empty required-looking fields and {F010} of sampled rows carry personal-data markers. Three grade C product candidates lead, and each needs de-identification or aggregation first. Rights are settled by the owner's declaration, so that preparation is technical rather than legal.
